ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory baseline screening of every director, officer, and individual with significant control (ISC) against: (1) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (CASL) administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (2) Public Safety Canada's terrorist entity listing; (3) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (4) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists adopted as enhanced US counterparty risk control; and (5) domestic PEP categories covering foreign, domestic, and multinational politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, consistent with FINTRAC regulatory guidance. Given the Low_Risk_Standard product tier, screening must be refreshed at least annually or upon any change in ownership or control; any adverse hit requires enhanced due diligence, a written escalation memorandum to the compliance officer, and, where legally triggered, reporting to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), accessible at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry via authorized service providers using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s 10 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), the corporate name must be in English, French, or both, and must contain a statutory legal element (Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, Ltd., Inc., Corp., or a recognized French equivalent). The name must produce a distinct NUANS report and must not be confusingly similar to any existing federal, provincial, or foreign registered name or trademark. Names in non-Latin scripts must be translated or transliterated into Latin characters and must not create confusion with existing Alberta or Canadian names. The Registrar will reject names that are obscene, contrary to public interest, or that imply Crown, government, or municipal patronage.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS rejection due to confusing similarity or a prohibited/sensitive token, the incorporator may: (1) obtain the written consent of the senior user or right holder and file it with the Registrar to permit coexistence; (2) submit a written re-evaluation request to the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, attaching the NUANS report and reasoned arguments on distinctiveness, use, or acquired goodwill; (3) if the Director affirms the rejection, apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). If the name is refused only because the reservation window expired, the applicant must obtain a fresh NUANS search report and file a new reservation, which may be extended by refiling before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only for the statutory corporate registered office, provided a physical street address in Alberta is maintained at which service of process can be accepted; a post office box alone is prohibited. For the manufacture of self-heating instant meals (ISIC 1079), a physical manufacturing establishment with a fixed address is mandatory under the Safe Food for Canadians Act and the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations, as well as municipal business licensing in Alberta; therefore a virtual office cannot satisfy the production facility requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For the registered office, the unannounced physical inspection risk is low (approximately 5% annual probability by Alberta Corporate Registry or law enforcement). For the food manufacturing establishment, the risk is moderate-to-high: the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Alberta Health Services (AHS) conduct routine and unannounced food safety establishment inspections, and for a novel self-heating food product category the estimated probability of a first on-site inspection within 12 months of licensing is approximately 70%.

Submit documents online with required consents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is queried or unavailable, amend name and resubmit within prescribed period to avoid rejection

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload completed Articles of Incorporation and supporting documents including director consents and initial statement to the Service Alberta portal. Include payment of filing fee. Monitor status for approval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Ottawa — national tax administration and agent of the Government of Alberta for corporate income tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act (RSA 2000 c C-21); federal GST administration under the Excise Tax Act (RSC 1985 c E-15). Portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/business-number-registration.html; CRA My Business Account; Alberta Corporate Registry at https://www.albertacorporate.com; CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) administers export declarations via eManifest and CARM/GCA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Business Corporation incorporated federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and carrying on business in Alberta: (1) file Articles of Incorporation, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, and comply with director-residency rules (ABCA requires a majority of resident Canadian directors; CBCA requires 25% resident Canadian directors); (2) obtain the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, and simultaneously open program accounts: RC (corporate income tax — dual federal/Alberta T2 filing), RT (GST/HST), RM (CBSA import/export), and RP (payroll if employees are engaged); (3) GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters or may be elected voluntarily under ETA s. 240(3); (4) if incorporated under the CBCA, complete extra-provincial registration in Alberta (EPC compliance) with the Alberta Corporate Registry; (5) file the annual T2 corporate income tax return within six months of each taxation year-end (electronic filing mandatory where gross revenue exceeds CAD 1 million) with GIFI and Alberta Schedule 5 allocation of taxable income to the Alberta permanent establishment, applying the 2% small-business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible income and 8% general Alberta rate; (6) maintain records in English or French for six years and disclose reportable cross-border transactions on Form T106 and foreign affiliates on Form T1134.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is a statutory resident of Canada under ITA s. 250(4)(a) and is taxed at the entity level on worldwide income (federal general rate 15%, federal small-business rate 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of CCPC income, plus Alberta general rate 8% and Alberta small-business rate 2%). It is the GST/HST registrant liable for 5% GST on taxable supplies; no pass-through or check-the-box flow-through election exists for a Canadian-incorporated corporation; non-resident shareholders derive income only as dividends subject to Part IV tax and dividend refund mechanics, and the corporation is the sole taxpayer on operating profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer a check-the-box regime for domestic corporations. Available statutory and administrative elections relevant to this structure include: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier under ETA s. 240(3) to claim input tax credits and effect export zero-rating; (ii) election under ITA s. 83(2) to deem dividends paid out of the capital dividend account as non-taxable; (iii) election under ITA s. 93(1) on dispositions of shares of foreign affiliates to access exempt surplus; (iv) designation of a foreign affiliate under ITA s. 5907(1) and related surplus computation elections; (v) treaty-residence deeming under ITA s. 250(6)/(4.1) where the Canada-United States treaty tie-breaker assigns residence to the United States, limiting Canadian taxation of the corporation to Canadian-source income; and (vi) hybrid-mismatch outcomes, which are mandatory and cannot be elected around — ITA ss. 18.4, 18.5 and 18.6 automatically deny or defer deductions arising from imported hybrid mismatches and other double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion arrangements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: All elections must be filed on prescribed CRA forms and within statutory deadlines; competent authority determinations under the treaty tie-breaker require a mutual-agreement procedure filing with CRA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax. Alberta is a non-participating province, so only the 5% federal Goods and Services Tax applies; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax and no provincial GST/HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — aggregate worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made by the person in Canada during any four consecutive calendar quarters, measured under the small-supplier rules of ETA s. 123(1) and the registration requirement of ETA s. 240(1). Once the threshold is exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory; a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must register only if carrying on business in Canada, subject to the same CAD 30,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently implement mandatory real-time e-invoice clearance, government fiscal stamping, or API pre-approval of invoices. Commercial invoices may be paper or electronic if they satisfy ETA s. 221(2) validation requirements (vendor name, BN/RT number, GST/HST charged). Mandatory digital compliance includes: (i) all GST/HST registrants must file GST/HST returns and remittances electronically via CRA GST/HST NETFILE or CRA-approved software for reporting periods beginning after 2022 (paper filing has been phased out); (ii) export declarations to the CBSA must be transmitted electronically through eManifest or CARM/GCA for commercial goods; (iii) zero-rating documentation must be retained in machine-readable format for at least six years; and (iv) any GST/HST net remittance exceeding CAD 10,000 must be remitted by electronic funds transfer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating arises under Schedule VI, s. 20 of the Excise Tax Act for supplies of goods manufactured in Canada and sold for export: the registrant must possess documentary evidence of physical export (contract, commercial invoice, CBSA export declaration, bill of lading or waybill); the goods must be shipped to a destination outside Canada and exported 'as soon as is reasonably possible' after delivery; and supplies made in Canada to non-resident purchasers for subsequent export may also be zero-rated where the goods are in fact exported within a reasonable time. For the Self-Heating Instant Hot Water Pot: when sold domestically in Alberta, the basic-food meal component may be zero-rated as basic groceries under Schedule VI, Part III, while the chemical self-heating pot and utensil components are taxable at 5% under composite-supply analysis; when the complete self-heating meal kit is exported, the entire assembled product, including the exothermic heating element and food carton, is zero-rated at 0% under s. 20. Ancillary services performed on or in respect of the exported goods, such as contract manufacturing, packaging, and freight, may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, ss. 21-23; the zero-rating applies to the whole composite supply where the predominant element is the exported good.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Invoice / Canada Customs Invoice stating 'Zero-Rated Export' and identifying the vendor's CRA BN/RT registration number
CBSA electronic export declaration: Canadian Export Reporting System transcript, eManifest screen print, or CARM/GCA portal confirmation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the Canadian manufacturer as shipper/exporter and proving delivery to a consignee outside Canada
Proof of Export: carrier terminal receipts, port or border clearance stamps, and third-party logistics warehouse certificates confirming physical exit of the goods from Canada
Order and customs valuation documentation enabling classification of the self-heating meal kit under the applicable HS codes and ISIC 1079 correspondence
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT MT103 credit advice / bank foreign-currency settlement confirmation evidencing foreign exchange repatriation within the 180-day settlement benchmark
GST/HST electronic return and supporting calculation schedule identifying zero-rated export sales separately for CRA reconciliation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA verifies export zero-rating claims by cross-matching GST/HST returns with CBSA export declarations, carrier manifests, customs broker records, and banking SWIFT inflows. Where documentation is deficient or false, CRA may reassess the supply as taxable at 5% in full, deny related input tax credits, and impose: (i) late-filing penalties under ETA s. 282 equal to 1% of the net tax due plus 0.25% per month up to 12 months; (ii) a 20% culpable-conduct penalty under ETA s. 285.1 for gross negligence in making false statements or omissions; (iii) a 100% penalty with a minimum CAD 2,000 under ETA s. 285 for false statements or wilful evasion; (iv) prescribed-rate interest compounded daily on the reassessed tax (2025 CRA rates approximately 8-10%); (v) criminal prosecution under ETA s. 289 with fines up to CAD 50,000 and imprisonment up to two years for knowing participation in export-fraud schemes; and (vi) retrospective clawbacks over the four-year normal reassessment period, extended to eight years where misrepresentation is established. Alberta may also reopen corporate income tax assessments where the permanent- establishment allocation was understated. Where export proceeds remain offshore beyond the 180-day benchmark, ITA ss. 17 and 247 empower CRA to impute deemed interest and make transfer-pricing adjustments, adding corporate tax, penalties, and interest to the indirect-tax clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting as fiscal agent of the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act; there is no standalone foreign-exchange control authority. Canadian banks are prudentially supervised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and all cross-border wire transfers are monitored by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible. Canada imposes no general exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions; profit remittances by way of dividends are freely permitted without Bank of Canada approval. Applicable constraints are fiscal rather than exchange-control: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (NR4) on dividends and interest, section 247 transfer-pricing documentation, section 18(4) thin-capitalization rules on debt-to-equity limits, and FINTRAC reporting of large cross-border transfers (CAD 10,000 or more). For a self-heating-food manufacturer, royalties for licensed chemical-thermal technology are also freely remittable subject to withholding tax and treaty relief (e.g., Canada–China, Canada–Korea protocols).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no requirement to repatriate foreign-currency receipts within a prescribed timeline. Exporters may open and retain foreign-currency accounts at Canadian banks. Reporting obligations apply only for statistical purposes: exports exceeding CAD 2,000 per shipment must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via the B13A Export Declaration, and aggregated data flows to Statistics Canada. Proceeds may be received in any currency and settled via the bank's correspondent network.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (conditional). Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer and Currencycloud are not licensed banks in Canada and cannot provide CDIC-insured deposit accounts, bankers' acceptances, or commercial letters of credit. They may operate in Canada only as registered money services businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC or, for payment services, under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) effective November 1, 2024. Recommended use: secondary collection and small-ticket vendor disbursement rail only. Primary liquidity and LC issuance must sit with a Schedule I Canadian bank. Alberta-based food exporters using EMIs as the sole treasury rail face significant compliance rejection at the banking level due to lack of regulatory capital and audit trail depth.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Canadian-resident President, CFO, or a director who is a Canadian resident must generally attend an in-person branch interview for the initial account opening. For non-resident directors and shareholders (permitted under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Alberta Business Corporations Act), banks accept notarized government-issued photo ID, proof of address, a corporate resolution, and a banking reference letter; remote opening may be permitted only through the bank's international desk (e.g., RBC Hong Kong, TD International, BMO China) or with an attestation executed before a notary public and legalized by a Canadian consulate. In practice, at least one physical meeting in Canada is required for the authorized signatory who will execute wire instructions, given the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier of the food-manufacturing sector. The corporation must maintain a registered Alberta office and a registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owners (BO) or shareholders holding 25% or more with no Canadian nexus, including an offshore parent or a distributor with opaque ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organizational chart; Alberta and federal corporate registry extracts; certificate of good standing for each BO; passport copies; proof of source of wealth and source of funds; completed CRS/FATCA self-certification (Form W-8BEN-E or W-9); signed board resolution naming all authorized signatories; beneficial ownership search report from an accredited registry agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use chemical inputs for the exothermic self-heating element (e.g., powdered aluminum, magnesium, calcium oxide) flagged under Canada's Export Control List or the Explosives Act screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Suppliers' Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS/SDS); chemical supplier commercial invoices and licenses; Health Canada and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) product approvals; food-contact-material compliance certificates; warehouse storage certification; written end-use statement confirming the chemicals are encapsulated exclusively as food-heating agents; no-use statement for explosives or pyrotechnic applications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires to/from China, Hong Kong, Vietnam, or Thailand (raw-material suppliers and contract packers) exceeding CAD 10,000 per transaction or CAD 50,000 within 24 hours
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply agreements with named counterparties; commercial invoices; bills of lading and packing lists; customs entry documentation (CBSA); LC and SWIFT message copies; FINTRAC-compliant reporting records; screening clearance confirming no OFAC/UN/Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List matches; internal AML/CFT procedures manual and training log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-velocity mismatch: forecasted export sales inconsistent with account activity for NAICS 311999 in the first 12 months, triggering enhanced review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reviewed financial statements (CPA-prepared); GST/HST return history and CRA Notices of Assessment; sales contracts and purchase orders from anchor retail distributors; production-capacity evidence; signed management representation letter; warehouse and logistics contracts; quality-certification records (e.g., SQF/BRCGS or CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act licence) substantiating operating reality.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and debt capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103/202 from the investing entity's own bank account to the Canadian beneficiary account, with the following compliance protocol: (i) reference the beneficiary bank SWIFT BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2 for RBC, TDOMCATTTOR for TD, NOSCCATT for Scotiabank, BOFMCAM2 for BMO, CIBCCATT for CIBC); (ii) include the beneficiary legal name and Alberta Registration Number; (iii) state purpose code for direct-investment equity injection (BPM6 code DI/611 or the receiving bank's equivalent capital-contribution code); (iv) attach a certified board resolution approving share issuance or shareholder loan; (v) provide a share-subscription agreement and, for parent-guarantee debt, an executed loan agreement. For inbound amounts greater than CAD 10,000, FINTRAC reporting is generated by the bank; amounts greater than CAD 50,000 in a 24-hour window trigger enhanced due-diligence verification and a likely compliance interview. USD-denominated injections clear via the bank's US correspondent through Fedwire or CHIPS into the USD account, after which spot conversion to CAD is optional and must be documented with a client FX dealing ticket.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw materials (self-heating containers, desiccants, food ingredients, packaging film) and contract manufacturing will use: (i) regular supplier payments via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer with full 56A/57A/59 beneficiary details and corresponding purpose code (e.g., trade payables); (ii) irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit (L/C at sight) for large shipments from Asia, issued by the Canadian bank, advised/confirmed through the seller's bank, with Incoterms 2020 (FOB or CIF) and required documents including commercial invoice, full-set clean-on-board bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, health certificate, and weight certificate; (iii) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for mid-risk suppliers; and (iv) domestic CAD disbursements through Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the emerging Real-Time Rail (RTR). USD outflows settle through the bank's US correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire); CAD cross-border wires use SWIFT with correspondent arrangements. All outbound transactions are subject to the bank's sanctions screening and to FINTRAC reporting above threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH) for 1–12 month tenors under a bank-documented ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Canadian FX Master Agreement
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted/Asian currencies (CNY, KRW, INR, THB, VND) to hedge raw-material import costs without physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) for medium-term hedging of shareholder loans and capital-structure exposure
FX options (plain vanilla calls/puts and zero-cost collars) purchased from the bank's global markets desk for risk-protected budget rates
Rolling FX forwards with monthly resettlement for continuous hedging of predictable export receivables in USD and EUR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Significant Individuals (beneficial owner) confirmation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the annual return date (anniversary of incorporation or of the last filed annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 50 (USD 37) once overdue; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers Registrar's s.213 ABCA dissolution procedure (notice, grace period, administrative strike-off); directors may incur statutory liability for debts contracted during strike-off period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax portions) with financial statements and required schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Calgary Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 6 months after the end of each taxation year (fiscal period anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (ITA s.162); gross negligence penalty of 50% (ITA s.163); compound daily interest at prescribed CRA rate; garnishment, director liability under ITA s.227.1, and prosecution in egregious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid and T4 Summary (annual employer information return for payroll calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid (February 28 or 29)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file information return penalty of CAD 100 per return plus CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 (ITA s.162); separate ITA s.227.1 director liability for unremitted payroll withholdings; e-filing mandatory for employers issuing over 50 T4 slips.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Alberta private corporations have no asset- or revenue-based statutory audit threshold. An independent auditor is required unless all shareholders unanimously consent to dispense with the auditor (ABCA s.151(5)), in which case an accountant's review engagement may satisfy record-keeping needs. Mandatory audits apply to reporting issuers, regulated financial intermediaries, and entities where lenders, CFIA licensing, or contractual covenants impose an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for public/reporting enterprises; ASPE (Part II) for private Canadian-controlled corporations. Either framework is accepted by CRA; the T2 return converts financial statement income to Income Tax Act basis under s.9 and applicable provisions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ABCA requires each corporation to maintain a Register of Significant Individuals (persons having 25% or more of voting rights, 25% or more of the fair market value of shares, or de facto control). The Annual Return mandates confirmation or update of Significant Individual information, certified by a director or officer. Any share transfer or control change must be recorded in the register within 15 days of knowledge; the year-end Annual Return then reconfirms the current UBO set.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual registered office and corporate secretarial package in Alberta: CAD 300-900 (USD 220-665); self-maintained office reduces this to mailing and address administration costs only.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Full independent audit if not waived: CAD 8,000-30,000 (USD 5,900-22,200); accountant's review engagement for a manufacturing SME where shareholder waiver applies: CAD 3,500-9,000 (USD 2,600-6,700).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined: 15% federal general corporate rate plus 8% Alberta general corporate rate (effective for Alberta taxation years beginning on or after 1 January 2020).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 11% combined preferential rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CA$500,000 of active business income for a qualifying Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) eligible for the Small Business Deduction; 35% fully refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit for CCPCs; 100% first-year Capital Cost Allowance full expensing for eligible manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment acquired and available for use before 2028; federal clean technology investment tax credits where applicable.
